description: pvpumpingsystem contains Python tools for modelling and sizing photovoltaic water-pumping installations. The package contributors publish it to help select pumping-station components against required water delivery and acceptable shortage risk. Its README describes hourly operation and technical and financial results over one year, with examples located in Tunis. The software is parameterised by the user, not confined to that demonstration location; transfer to other sites requires suitable local inputs. Source code is available from GitHub, with installation through pip and documentation on Read the Docs. GitHub states the GPL-3.0 licence, making the code free to reuse under its terms. The examples cover outflows, water-shortage probability and life-cycle cost, as well as component selection. These outputs can inform rural water-supply or irrigation capacity planning. Limitations include the hourly time step and the need to check the suitability of component assumptions for the proposed installation. Related record model-calliope covers broader energy-system planning, while this package addresses pumping-system design. Its examples were not run during this metadata review.
